cases.name: a bare null label
cases.why: a null label declares nothing, so the section takes the UI label for its content mode

cases.name: a tilde null label
cases.why: YAML spells null four ways and all of them declare nothing

cases.name: a spelled null label
cases.why: YAML spells null four ways and all of them declare nothing

cases.name: a shouted null label
cases.why: YAML spells null four ways and all of them declare nothing

cases.name: the straddle partner: an unquoted None, a string in YAML
cases.why: YAML has no None literal, so this is the four-letter string, and a declared label is printed as written

cases.name: the straddle partner, quoted
cases.why: quoting changes nothing: the declared label is the string None and is printed as written

cases.name: a label of U+001E only, whitespace under Python
cases.why: U+001E is whitespace to Python, so the declared label is blank and declares nothing

cases.name: a label padded with U+001E, WP-5.1f's case
cases.why: padding is stripped and ARTICLE remains; kept from WP-5.1f, but its value collides with the fallback so it cannot tell the two branches apart on its own

cases.name: a label padded with U+001E, distinguishable from the fallback
cases.why: padding is stripped and Dispatch remains; unlike the case above, this value is not the fallback, so it proves the declared branch was taken

cases.name: control: an ordinary label
cases.why: a declared label is printed as written

cases.name: control: an ASCII-space-padded label
cases.why: ASCII space is whitespace to both languages, so this agreed before any fix and still does

cases.name: control: an empty string, which is not null
cases.why: an empty declared label declares nothing, by the same rule as a blank one, and reaches the fallback without needing the null guard

cases.name: class C: a boolean scalar prints False in both engines
cases.why: pinned as the behaviour both engines have, NOT as a correct value: Python guards on value is not None and False is not None, so it stringifies. Parity cannot see this, because the two engines agree on it. Changing it would change the Python oracle, which is a plan-level decision and not this WP's.
